headline: Two runs back-to-back now — the restart is real, not a one-off. Both carried genuine top-end range. Strength is still the quietest corner of the picture.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: Two runs in short succession finally turn a single data point into a rhythm, and both landed with real intensity through the upper zones rather than easy shakeouts — a distinct shift from the huge, deliberately slow trail block that preceded them. The contrast is stark: the Åre and Krokom efforts were massive time-on-feet at conversational effort, and these two are short and sharp. That's a healthy pairing for hybrid capacity, but it also means the recent 4-week volume figure is inflated by the trail block and doesn't reflect where load sits right now. Strength remains the laggard — a single session in the last stretch, no weekly frame, and the most recent one logged no HR. Steps stay genuinely high even on rest days, so the background aerobic drip is intact regardless of what the run log shows. The strain reading sitting at zero reflects the recent light stretch more than any true deconditioning; the base underneath is deep.
sections.trends: Year-to-date distance is roughly four times where it stood at this point last year, which tells you the annual trajectory is firmly upward regardless of any short-term quiet patch. The shape within the last few months is cyclical rather than linear: a large trail-durability block, a genuine off-stretch, and now a speed-flavoured restart. That oscillation fits the standing goal of maintaining both endurance and top-end year-round — it's not drift, it's the two qualities taking turns. The thing to keep honest is that the loading side (strength) hasn't cycled back up with the running yet.
sections.threshold: The threshold figure is now the oldest metric on the board by a wide margin, and nothing in the last two runs was a sustained tempo or threshold effort — they touched the upper zones in bursts but didn't hold a controlled hard steady state long enough to refresh it. So the current threshold number should be treated as a stale estimate, not a live reading. Given the depth of base and the intensity these runs are already showing, the underlying fitness is very plausibly intact or better, but that remains an inference until a genuine sustained effort confirms it.
sections.zones: The weekly aggregate is skewed by the trail block's enormous Z1 accumulation, so it looks almost entirely low-intensity — but the per-session shapes tell the real recent story. Both restart runs spent meaningful time in Z3 with a touch of Z4, which is exactly the kind of upper-range stimulus that was absent for weeks. That's appropriate for reopening speed capacity after a long slow block. What's missing isn't intensity, it's a controlled threshold-length effort — the runs are ranging through zones in bursts rather than parking in one deliberately.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing new to note on strength HR — the most recent session logged none at all, so there's still no fresh reading on how hard the lifting is running. The prior lifts sat sensibly in the low-to-moderate range, consistent with functional-fitness circuits rather than heavy grind work. No source-agreement concerns worth flagging on the run side.
sections.calendar: The running side has clearly re-engaged after the gap, and the tight spacing of the two runs is the more telling signal than any single session — it's the first evidence of frequency returning rather than an isolated re-entry. Strength, by contrast, shows no such clustering; it remains scattered singles with no repeating weekly slot, which is the one consistency pattern that hasn't recovered.
sections.personal_bests: The short-distance PBs were set almost exactly a year ago, in the same late-August window — worth noting given the athlete is now returning to sharper running at the same point in the calendar. Nothing in the last two runs is at PB pace, but the top-end range reappearing is the raw material those bests are built from. It's early to talk realistic reach; a couple more sharp sessions and one genuine threshold effort would make that a real conversation.

watch_items: Watch whether the run frequency holds into a third and fourth session — two runs confirm a restart, but not yet a sustained weekly cadence.
Watch for a controlled sustained tempo or threshold effort, since the burst-style intensity so far hasn't refreshed the oldest metric on the board.
Watch whether strength finally clusters into a repeating weekly slot rather than staying isolated singles.
Watch whether the next lift captures HR, so the intensity of the strength work stops being a blind spot.
